title: Drill-down: religion to Christianity to the resurrection
description: Two friends start on religion in general (why people believe at all), narrow to Christianity specifically, then to whether the resurrection accounts are historical. Expect a broad religion/faith anchor and a Christianity node with the resurrection nested beneath it as a child.

utterances.text: Can I ask you something kind of personal? Do you actually still believe in God, or is church more of a family thing for you now?
Honestly it's both. I think most people believe because of where they grew up, and I'm not sure I'm different.
That's what gets me though. If you'd been born in Jakarta you'd probably be Muslim, so how can any one religion be the true one?
Sure, but that argument cuts both ways. If you'd been born in Copenhagen you'd probably be an atheist, and you wouldn't say that makes atheism false.
Okay, fair. I guess I just think belief is mostly comfort. People want something to hold onto when things go wrong.
Some of it is comfort, for sure. But a lot of the people I know at church believe because of specific stuff, not just a warm feeling.
Like what, though? What's the specific stuff for you, for Christianity in particular?
For me it's mostly Jesus. Like, the person. The way he treated people nobody else would touch, lepers, tax collectors, women in that culture.
I mean I'll give you that he was an impressive moral teacher. Plenty of atheists say that too.
Right, but C.S. Lewis has that line, that he didn't leave that option open. He claimed to forgive sins, he talked like he was God.
Or the gospel writers put those words in his mouth decades later. Mark was written what, forty years after?
Something like that, yeah. But Paul's letters are earlier, and he's already worshipping Jesus within twenty years.
Okay so what about the resurrection itself. Do you think that literally happened, like a dead body got up?
Yeah, I actually do. And it's the whole thing, Paul says if Christ isn't raised your faith is useless.
But what's the evidence beyond the Bible saying so? That's kind of circular.
The usual argument is the empty tomb plus the appearances. Women found the tomb, and in that culture women weren't credible witnesses, so why make that up?
Huh. I hadn't heard that one. That's actually a decent point about the women.
And then the disciples went from hiding to dying for it. People don't usually die for something they know they invented.
People die for false things all the time though. Heaven's Gate, whatever. Sincerity isn't evidence.
Sure, but they'd be the ones who knew whether they saw him. That's different from believing something secondhand.
Maybe it was grief hallucinations. You lose someone and you see them everywhere for months. My mom saw my grandpa in the kitchen.
That's the best skeptical explanation, I think. But it doesn't really explain five hundred people at once, or the empty tomb.
If the five hundred thing is even real. That's one line in one letter.
Fair. I'm not saying it proves it. I just think it's harder to explain away than people assume.
